brief.headline: Offer to pay 15 days faster in exchange for a 4% price cut — worth ₹1.13 Cr/yr to us — and line up Huhtamaki or UFLEX as a backup.

priceAsk.summary: Ask for ₹290/KG on the three main items — roughly 4% off our current price — by matching Shrinath Roto Pack's rate.
priceAsk.basis: Shrinath Roto Pack already supplies those items at ₹290/KG; market research shows ₹205–305/kg is fair, with ₹250/kg typical, so our current ₹294–308/KG sits at the top of the band and ₹290 is still market-fair.

paymentTermAsk.summary: Move from 30 days to 15 days after receipt — in exchange for the price cut above.
paymentTermAsk.cashImpact: Frees up ₹1.16 Cr of our cash that's sitting with them.

brief.financialLeverage: They bring in ₹291.36 Cr a year and keep only 1.1% as profit — very little room to squeeze on price alone. But their cash is stuck for 81 days, longer than similar firms (46 days), so paying them faster is valuable to them. We buy ₹28.31 Cr/yr — 9.72% of everything they sell — so we're a big customer they can't afford to lose. Their credit rating is CRISIL BB+ / Stable, but they stopped sharing info with the rating agency, and they have GST filing delays, EPF payment delays, and pending legal cases — so treat their health as uncertain and keep a second source ready.

evidence.point: We pay ₹294.03–308.30/KG; Shrinath Roto Pack charges ₹290.00/KG for the same items
Matching Shrinath's price saves us ₹32.69 L a year
Market research shows pharma/ORS sachet laminate asks are ₹205–305/kg, typically ₹250/kg — our price is at the top
Their cash is stuck for 81 days, much longer than similar firms (46 days) — so they need cash
We're 9.72% of their revenue (₹28.31 Cr of ₹291.36 Cr) — a big slice they want to keep
Paying 15 days earlier frees ₹1.16 Cr of our cash; they borrow at 1.55-9.25% so early payment is worth that much to them

alternates.name: Huhtamaki India Ltd
alternates.why: Listed flexible-packaging converter (already a tiny FDC supplier, revenue ₹2755.75 Cr) — proven and scalable for laminate sachets; health C (58/100).

alternates.name: UFLEX Ltd
alternates.why: Listed flexibles giant (revenue ₹16492.00 Cr) — makes both film and finished laminates, so can match GEEP's range at scale; health C (46/100).

alternates.name: Constantia Parikh Packaging Pvt Ltd
alternates.why: Global Constantia group's India converter (revenue ₹222.04 Cr) — does pharma blister/sachet laminates; health D (31/100) but strong parent.

risks: GEEP supplies 76% of our Laminates (₹28.31 Cr) — we have almost no backup right now, so any disruption hits us hard; get a second source approved before pushing too hard.

Their rating is CRISIL BB+ / Stable, but they stopped cooperating with CRISIL, have GST filing delays, EPF payment delays, and pending legal cases — treat their health as shaky and don't assume the rating is current.
They keep only 1.1% as profit, much thinner than similar firms (2.1%) — a big price cut could hurt their ability to deliver; win on payment speed and volume certainty, not just price.
They have ₹-1.64 Cr free cash flow (negative) and a low Probe42 score (3/10) — watch for any signs of delivery trouble and have Huhtamaki or UFLEX ready to step in.
brief.suggestedOpeningLine: We value the partnership, but we're paying ₹294–308/KG while Shrinath gives us ₹290 for the same items — let's talk about closing that gap and how paying you faster can help both of us.
